rationale: The cap is 200 percent of the median and no unit rents above 140 percent, so the cap sits above the prices the market reaches and does not bind.
evidence: The ordinance caps the rent of every rental unit at 200 percent of the city's median rent on 1 January 2030.
No unit in the city currently rents for more than 140 percent of the median.

rationale: With the cap above current rents most landlords have no reason to exceed it, and the Rent Board can fine violators; enforcement detail is thin but compliance is likely.
evidence: The Rent Board enforces the cap and may fine landlords who exceed it.
